original.target_description: Study 4: averaged emotional attachment to siblings, parents and hometown following spatial priming. Source contains a three-group ANOVA and a closeness-versus-distance linear contrast; the supplied comparison description does not uniquely distinguish them. No conventional p is printed for either.

p.location: Printed p. 306 (source page 5), Study 4, Results and Discussion
p.quote: of their bonds to their family and hometown, F(2, 81) 5 4.97, ... prep 5 .95, Z2 5 .11. Again, using the contrast weights established ... primed with closeness (M 5 5.61), t(81) 5 2.86, prep 5 .96.

notes: Identity verified from supplied full article text: Keeping One’s Distance: The Influence of Spatial Distance Cues on Affect and Evaluation, Lawrence E. Williams and John A. Bargh, Yale University; Psychological Science, volume 19, number 3, pp. 302–308, copyright 2008. Title, authors, journal, year and pagination match the neutral original reference; DOI is not printed in the supplied text. Primary research article with four studies, methods, results and references; not an abstract or secondary report. No PDF was supplied. Only original pval_value_o is assigned; other fields and replication are null placeholders. Study 4 reports ANOVA F(2,81)=4.97 with p_rep=.95 and printed eta-squared=.11, linear contrast t(81)=2.86 with p_rep=.96, and quadratic contrast t(81)=1.36, n.s. These are candidate tests, not inferred target assignments. Conventional p values and numerical p bounds are not printed for the ANOVA or linear contrast. p_rep is retained as a distinct printed measure, not converted into p. No target selected from input order or numeric agreement. Target correspondence between omnibus and linear contrast remains unresolved (target_ambiguous); the absence of conventional p applies to both. No N or effect size extracted because they are unassigned.
